claims.statement: hypermnesic ships three independent agent-integration surfaces — the Claude Code/Codex MCP pack under plugin/plugins/hypermnesic/, the Hermes CLI pack under plugin/hermes/, and an Obsidian companion maintained in a separate repository — and the Hermes pack deliberately consumes neither the Claude/Codex manifests nor their MCP wiring.

The bundled MCP wiring is OAuth-discovery-only: it declares a streamable-http server whose URL is templated from HYPERMNESIC_MCP_URL with a placeholder default, and carries no auth block and no static Authorization header, because a static header would suppress the host's OAuth Authorization Server discovery.

The Claude Code/Codex plugin registers exactly one hook event, UserPromptSubmit, invoking hypermnesic_agent_hook.py with a per-host flag and a 6-second timeout; there is no SessionStart preamble and no Bash interception.

The auto-recall hook can never block or fail a turn: every code path returns {"continue": true}, context is added only through hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, a malformed JSON payload still emits a continue response, and any non-prompt-submit event is inert.

The hook applies an ordered set of cheap gates before any network call — disabled state, prompt relevance (memory-ish phrasing or a multi-word proper noun), a configured endpoint URL, an available credential, and a non-empty query — so an off-topic or unconfigured prompt costs no request.

Because the agent host exposes no stored MCP OAuth token to hook subprocesses, the hook cannot reuse the app's OAuth login; HYPERMNESIC_MCP_TOKEN is optional, used only in the Authorization header and never printed or injected, and the hook's credential-free remote path is the tailnet read companion, which needs only a URL.

The hook's recall is bounded on every axis: a single JSON-RPC tools/call to the search tool with k=5 under a 2.5-second timeout, at most five hits rendered, each snippet trimmed to 200 characters with newlines flattened so note content cannot forge structure inside the injected block.

Every hook run resolves to one of a fixed set of stable outcome codes — never_run, off_topic, disabled_global, disabled_host, unconfigured_endpoint, missing_credential, auth_expired, timeout, lookup_failed, no_hits, degraded_lexical_only, success — each paired with a plain-language explanation, which is what makes the hook's designed silence diagnosable.

The hook status record stores derived categories rather than values — the endpoint reduced to local, tailnet_read, public_https, other, or unset and the credential to token_present, not_required_tailnet, or missing — and never stores the full prompt, the endpoint URL, the token, the Authorization header, or raw large snippets.

Status persistence is best-effort and non-blocking: the write is wrapped so an unwritable path is swallowed rather than failing the hook, and an absent status file reads back as the never_run outcome instead of an error.

Proactive recall can be disabled without uninstalling the plugin or removing MCP tools, globally with HYPERMNESIC_HOOK_DISABLE_LOOKUP=1 or per host with a comma-separated HYPERMNESIC_HOOK_DISABLED_HOSTS, and both checks run before relevance evaluation.

The status helper's test-recall mode runs the same bounded lookup for an explicit query, prints sanitized path/heading/snippet previews, and marks the persisted record test_initiated so a diagnostic run stays distinguishable from real hook traffic.

The Hermes pack is CLI-first rather than MCP-based: it requires only HYPERMNESIC_REPO, shells out to the local hypermnesic retrieve command with --json, and a test asserts the package carries no MCP transport or Claude/Codex loader assumptions.
In the Hermes pack the memory skill is always registered but the pre_llm_call recall hook is opt-in, registered only when HYPERMNESIC_HERMES_RECALL is set to a truthy value.

The Hermes recall hook is bounded to at most three hits under a 3-second subprocess timeout with injected context capped at 1400 characters, and returns silence on every failure mode including an irrelevant message, an unset repository, a subprocess error, a non-zero exit, unparseable JSON, or no hits.

The repository carries two marketplace manifests on purpose because Claude Code discovers marketplace.json only at a checkout root; the root manifest lists only the plugin name and source while version and description live solely in the plugin manifest, so a version bump touches one file and the manifests cannot drift.

The Obsidian companion ships from a separate public repository under GPL-3.0-or-later while the engine here is AGPL-3.0-only, and the arm's-length boundary rests on them being separate processes communicating solely over the read-only MCP wire (search, build_context, think) — a conditional that holds only while the companion does not vendor, import, or statically link engine source.

The Obsidian companion is a read-only review and navigation surface: write, cleanup, revoke, forget, and revert stay in the git-first CLI/MCP surfaces, and a read-only client cannot bypass consent, write scope, protected-path refusals, or server-side write guards.

Both plugin skill files carry the same memory-taxonomy routing rule — durable project memory belongs in hypermnesic while behavioural preferences and temporary session state belong in an adjacent behavioural layer — and instruct agents to preserve raw evidence, call list_folders when the destination is unclear, and treat write refusals as control signals rather than bypass targets.

The plugin distribution is kept operator-neutral by test: the plugin tree is asserted to contain no committed secrets and no operator-specific hostnames or values, which is what makes the same artifacts installable by any operator.
